patients.summary: Healthy financial analyst who joined in 2023, developed exertional dyspnea and dry cough in mid-2024 and was diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis by pulmonary in January 2025. He progressed to bilateral lung transplantation in May 2026 and was treated for CMV pneumonitis two months later; the practice last saw him in October 2025 and has filed the transplant records since.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller would like to establish care. His previous primary care doctor retired over the summer and the office closed. Works from home most days, flexible schedule. Explained membership, same-day access and that insurance still covers labs and specialists. Booked new patient appt 9/12 at 8:30. Records release form emailed; he will sign and send back so we can request his old chart.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
54M here to establish. Prior PCP retired; records requested.

Feels well. No complaints today. Exercises a few times a week, mostly walking and a stationary bike. Sleeps fine. Denies breathing problems, cough, palpitations, GI or urinary symptoms.

PMH: none he knows of. No surgeries. Meds: none, no supplements. NKDA.
Family: father had interstitial lung disease; mother has rheumatoid arthritis. He is not sure of the details of his father's illness.
Social: financial analyst, mostly remote. Divorced, lives alone in Easthampton. Lifelong nonsmoker. Alcohol 1-2 drinks a week. No drug use.
Prevention per patient: colonoscopy around age 50, told normal. Tetanus shot within the last several years. Never had shingles vaccine.

Exam: well appearing. Vitals as charted. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no nodes or thyromegaly. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally, good air movement. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema. Skin without concerning lesions. PHQ-2 0.

Assessment / plan:
1. Health maintenance, healthy adult. Baseline CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c. Hep C and HIV screen once, discussed and he agrees.
2. Colon screening: confirm date of colonoscopy from old records.
3. Vaccines: flu and COVID when the fall supply arrives. Shingrix discussed, will start next year at his physical.
RTC one year, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Lloyd, all of your bloodwork from Tuesday came back normal: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, sugar/A1c and cholesterol. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. Nothing to change. Good to meet you.

documents.title: Prior primary care records
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
41 pages received from the prior primary care office (closed practice, records custodian). Summary abstracted for the chart:
- Screening colonoscopy 02/19/2019, average risk: normal exam, no polyps. Repeat in 10 years.
- Tdap 04/02/2019.
- Annual physicals 2016-2022, labs within normal limits each year.
- No chronic problems listed. No medications. No known drug allergies.
Originals in media tab.

documents.title: Vaccine visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In after work for flu and COVID. Screening questions negative, no prior reactions. Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM left arm. COVID 2023-24 formula 0.3 mL IM right arm. Observed 15 min, felt fine, left ambulatory.

documents.title: Shingles shot question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Morning. A coworker just had shingles and it sounded miserable. Can I get the vaccine before my physical or should I wait until June?

documents.title: Re: Shingles shot question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Either is fine. It's a two-shot series 2 to 6 months apart. If we give the first one at your physical in June, the second lines up nicely with your flu shot in October. Your arm may be sore for a day or two after each.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. 55 y/o man, no interval issues. Walking most mornings, bike on weekends. Busy quarter at work but sleeping OK. Denies shortness of breath, cough, chest discomfort, palpitations, weight change, bowel or urinary changes.

Meds none. NKDA. Never smoker, alcohol 1-2/wk.

Exam: NAD. Vitals reviewed. Eyes, ears, throat normal. No lymphadenopathy. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear to auscultation throughout. Abdomen benign. Extremities without edema or clubbing. Skin clear. PHQ-2 0.

Plan:
- Labs: CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c.
- Shingrix #1 given today, #2 in the fall with flu shot.
- Colonoscopy 2019 normal, next due 2029.
- Tdap current (2019).
Follow up in a year.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lloyd, labs from your physical are all in the normal range again. Cholesterol is fine. See you in the fall for shingles shot #2.

documents.title: Vaccine visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Lunch-hour visit for Shingrix dose 2, flu and 2024-25 COVID. First Shingrix dose in June gave him a sore arm for a day, nothing else. Shingrix L deltoid, flu R deltoid, COVID R deltoid lower site. Lot numbers in immunization record. Waited 15 minutes, no reaction. Shingrix series now complete.

documents.title: Breathing
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I've been meaning to ask about this for a while. Since around summer I get out of breath going up the one flight to my office, and I've had a dry cough that won't quit. Tried cough syrup and lozenges, nothing touches it. No fever. Probably nothing but I'd like to get it looked at.

documents.title: Re: Breathing
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Thanks for writing in. Doctor would like to see you in person rather than over messages. We have Tuesday 12/10 at 3:00. If you get short of breath at rest, chest pain, or lips turning blue before then, call 911. I've booked you, reply here if the time doesn't work.

orders.reason: exertional dyspnea, dry cough, bibasilar crackles

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Lloyd comes in about breathing. Roughly five months now (started around July) of getting winded on a single flight of stairs, which he never used to notice. Along with it a dry, hacking cough most days. OTC cough syrups and lozenges have not helped. No wheeze, no sputum, no chest pain, no leg swelling, no fevers. No orthopnea. Never smoked. No birds, mold or hobby exposures he can think of; desk job. Not on any medications.
Father had some kind of interstitial lung disease, which he mentions himself today and which is why he is worried.

Exam: comfortable at rest, speaking full sentences. SpO2 95% on room air at rest. Afebrile. Heart regular, no murmur, no JVD. Lungs: fine crackles at both bases, end-inspiratory, otherwise clear, no wheeze. No clubbing. No edema.

A/P: subacute exertional dyspnea with dry cough and bibasilar crackles in a never smoker with a family history of ILD. Concern for an interstitial process.
- CXR PA/lateral
- CBC, BMP today
- Pulmonology referral placed now, will expedite depending on film
- Return or call sooner if worse, any rest dyspnea or fever

reports.text:
CHEST, PA AND LATERAL
Indication: exertional dyspnea, dry cough, bibasilar crackles.
Comparison: none.
Findings: The heart is normal in size. Mediastinal and hilar contours are within normal limits. There is a subtle interstitial pattern, predominantly at the lung bases. No focal consolidation. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Osseous structures are unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Subtle interstitial pattern, predominantly at the lung bases. Further evaluation with high-resolution CT may be considered.

documents.title: Results call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt. Reviewed CXR: subtle changes at both lung bases, fits with the crackles I heard. Blood counts and chemistries normal. Explained this needs a lung specialist and probably a detailed CT and breathing tests; I've asked pulmonary to see him soon. Their office will call him. He asked whether this could be what his father had. Told him honestly that it's possible and that's exactly what the workup will sort out. He has my cell for anything in the meantime.

documents.title: Pulmonology referral
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Referral faxed to outside pulmonary group with 12/10 note, CXR report and labs. Marked priority. Pulmonary scheduling confirmed receipt; new patient appt offered 01/23/2025, pt accepted.

events.reason: dyspnea and dry cough, abnormal chest X-ray

reports.text:
HIGH-RESOLUTION CT CHEST WITHOUT CONTRAST, supine and prone, inspiratory and expiratory images.
Indication: exertional dyspnea, dry cough, basilar interstitial pattern on radiograph.
Comparison: chest radiograph 12/12/2024.
Findings: Reticulonodular opacities with a peripheral and basal predominance. Subpleural honeycombing at the lung bases. Opacities persist on prone images. No consolidation. No pleural effusion. Central airways patent. Heart size normal, no pericardial effusion. No mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy by size criteria. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Peripheral and basal predominant reticulonodular opacities with subpleural honeycombing, consistent with a usual interstitial pneumonia pattern.

documents.title: Pulmonary consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE PULMONARY & CRITICAL CARE CONSULTATION
Date of service: 01/23/2025
Referred by: primary care physician

Reason: half a year of worsening breathlessness and a dry cough.

History: Mr. Jacobs is a 56-year-old financial analyst who now gets winded climbing one flight of stairs. The cough is dry and persistent and has not responded to over-the-counter remedies. He has no wheeze, no sputum, no chest pain and no leg swelling. No occupational exposures. No recent travel and no known tuberculosis contact.

PMH: none. PSH: none. Medications: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father had interstitial lung disease; mother has rheumatoid arthritis.
Social: never smoker; 1 to 2 drinks per week.

Exam: Fine inspiratory crackles at both bases. No wheezes. No signs of volume overload; JVP not elevated. Heart regular with normal sounds. No peripheral edema. No clubbing.
Oxygen saturation 94% on room air at rest. Six-minute walk test: saturation fell to 88% on room air with exertion.

Data:
- Chest radiograph from his PCP (12/12/2024): subtle basilar-predominant interstitial pattern.
- HRCT today: reticulonodular opacities, peripheral and basal, with subpleural honeycombing.
- Pulmonary function tests today: TLC 66% predicted, FVC 68% predicted, FEV1/FVC 0.83, DLCO 51% predicted. Restriction with reduced diffusing capacity; no obstruction.
- Serologies today: ANA negative, RF negative, anti-CCP negative.

Impression: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. UIP pattern on HRCT, no exposures, no drug cause, and no evidence of connective tissue disease. The family history of ILD in his father is noted.

Recommendations:
1. Discussed the diagnosis and its usual course at length. Antifibrotic therapy recommended; we will review options at his return visit next month.
2. Ambulatory oxygen assessment given exertional desaturation; oxygen to be arranged with exertion.
3. Repeat PFTs in about 6 months.
4. Pneumococcal and annual influenza vaccination per PCP.

Thank you for this referral.
Pulmonary & Critical Care

documents.title: Pulmonary consult reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pulm letter came in yesterday. Dx idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: HRCT UIP pattern with honeycombing, restrictive PFTs, desats to 88% walking, serologies negative. Added IPF to problem list.
Called Lloyd. He had already heard it from pulmonary and has been reading online, which scared him. Talked through what we know and that the antifibrotic medicines slow it down. He is going back to pulm 2/27 to start treatment. Offered to see him any time to talk more. Will plan pneumococcal vaccine at his next visit here.

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth twice daily about 12 hours apart with food

documents.title: Pulmonary follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Pulmonary & Critical Care - follow-up letter
Visit 02/27/2025

Dear colleague,
I saw Mr. Jacobs back to plan treatment for his idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. Symptoms unchanged since January. We reviewed the two available antifibrotic agents and chose nintedanib 150 mg twice daily with food, to be dispensed through the specialty pharmacy once authorization clears. Common GI effects and the need for liver test monitoring were reviewed; our office will check liver enzymes monthly for the first three months and then every three months.

Based on his walk test he qualifies for ambulatory oxygen. He will use 2 L/min by portable concentrator with exertion; none needed at rest.

Pulmonary rehabilitation information given. Next visit with full PFTs in about five months.

Medications: nintedanib 150 mg BID (new); oxygen 2 L/min with exertion.
Allergies: NKDA

Pulmonary & Critical Care

documents.body: Specialty pharmacy faxed a request for recent clinic notes to support the nintedanib authorization started by pulmonary. Sent 12/10/24 office note and CXR report per release on file. Pulmonary office is handling the PA itself; FYI to PCP.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u after his IPF diagnosis. Started nintedanib early March after the authorization went through; taking it twice a day with meals and tolerating it. Uses the portable concentrator at 2 L when walking or on stairs, not at rest. Breathing about the same as in December, cough unchanged. Still working full time from home.
Mood: understandably anxious about the diagnosis, sleeping alright, not depressed. Has been reading less online, which helps.

Meds: nintedanib 150 mg BID (pulm). O2 2 L with exertion.
NKDA.

Exam: no distress at rest. SpO2 94% RA sitting. Heart RRR. Lungs with fine bibasilar crackles, unchanged. No clubbing, no edema.

A/P
IPF on nintedanib, followed by pulmonary.
- CMP today; pulm is also following LFTs, will forward to them
- PCV20 today
- Flu every fall
- Discussed that pulmonary may bring up transplant evaluation down the line; he has heard of it and wants to take things one step at a time
RTC 2-3 months.

orders.reason: idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis with declining FVC and DLCO

documents.title: Pulmonary follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Pulmonary & Critical Care - interval note to PCP
Date of service: 07/24/2025

IPF, on nintedanib 150 mg twice daily since March with good tolerance; monthly liver tests have been normal.
He reports that stairs are a little harder than in winter. Uses oxygen 2 L/min with exertion.
Resting saturation 93% on room air. Fine bibasilar crackles.

PFTs today: FVC 61% predicted (68% in January), DLCO 44% predicted (51% in January).

Assessment: idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis with measurable decline over six months despite antifibrotic therapy.
Plan:
- Continue nintedanib and exertional oxygen.
- Referral placed to a lung transplant center for evaluation. Discussed with him that early referral is standard in IPF and does not commit him to anything.
- Return in 4 months.

Pulmonary & Critical Care

documents.title: Lung transplant evaluation, initial visit
documents.author: lung transplant
documents.body:
LUNG TRANSPLANT PROGRAM - initial evaluation visit 09/18/2025

Mr. Jacobs, 56, referred by his pulmonologist for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis diagnosed in January 2025, on nintedanib with exertional oxygen at 2 L/min. FVC 61% and DLCO 44% predicted in July, both lower than at diagnosis. Never smoker, light alcohol use, no other medical problems, no prior surgery, NKDA.

We met with him today and began the formal candidacy evaluation (cardiac, imaging, laboratory, nutrition, social work and financial review over the coming weeks).

Request to primary care: please send documentation of age-appropriate cancer screening and his vaccination history, and confirm that he is due for this season's influenza and COVID vaccines. A form is enclosed.

Lung Transplant Program

Here for IPF check-in and the transplant program's paperwork.

Interval: pulmonary in July showed FVC and DLCO lower than in January; referred to transplant, first evaluation visit 9/18, more testing being scheduled by them. Still on nintedanib BID, tolerating it. Oxygen 2 L with exertion. Stairs slower. Cough the same. Working, fewer hours in the office building.
Mood okay. PHQ-2 1. Says having a plan helps.

Meds: nintedanib 150 mg BID (pulmonary). O2 2 L/min with exertion.
NKDA.

Exam: SpO2 93% RA at rest. Heart regular. Fine crackles both bases. No clubbing or edema.

Assessment and plan
1. IPF under pulmonary care, transplant evaluation in progress.
2. Transplant center form completed: colonoscopy 2019 normal (next 2029); Tdap 2019; Shingrix x2 2024; PCV20 4/2025; flu and COVID given today. Hep C and HIV screens negative 2023. Will fax with today's labs once back.
3. Labs: CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c.
4. Flu (L arm) and 2025-26 COVID (R arm) given today.
I'll see him back in the spring, sooner if anything changes; he will keep us posted on the transplant process.

documents.title: Labs and transplant form

documents.title: Lung transplant evaluation summary
documents.author: lung transplant
documents.body:
LUNG TRANSPLANT PROGRAM - evaluation summary, visit 12/11/2025

Diagnosis: idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (dx 01/2025), on nintedanib 150 mg twice daily; oxygen 2 L/min with exertion.

Repeat PFTs: FVC 55% predicted, DLCO 38% predicted, continuing the decline from 61% and 44% in July.
The remainder of the candidacy evaluation is complete without contraindication; thank you for the screening and vaccine documentation.

The selection committee has accepted Mr. Jacobs as a candidate for bilateral lung transplantation. Listing will follow once insurance authorization is finalized. Pulmonary will continue his routine IPF care in the meantime.

Lung Transplant Program

documents.title: Notification of transplant listing
documents.author: lung transplant
documents.body:
LUNG TRANSPLANT PROGRAM
Re: Lloyd Jacobs, DOB 10/26/1968

This is to notify you that as of 01/22/2026 your patient is active on the waiting list for bilateral lung transplantation for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. He has been instructed to keep his phone on at all times and to remain within travel distance of the center. He continues nintedanib and exertional oxygen through his pulmonologist while waiting.

Please let our coordinators know of any hospitalization, infection, new medication or vaccine while he is listed.

Lung Transplant Program

documents.title: Transplant discharge summary
documents.author: lung transplant
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - Lung Transplant Service
Admitted: 05/19/2026  Discharged: 06/02/2026

Admission diagnosis: idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, organ offer accepted.
Procedure: bilateral lung transplantation, 05/19/2026.

Hospital course: Called in overnight for a donor offer and taken to the operating room the same day. The operation was completed without complication. He was extubated early, transferred out of the ICU on schedule, and progressed steadily with physical therapy. Chest tubes were removed before discharge. The postoperative course was uneventful.

At discharge he is on room air, walking the unit independently.

Discharge medications:
- Tacrolimus 2 mg by mouth twice daily; goal trough 8-12 ng/mL, adjusted by the transplant team
- Mycophenolate mofetil 750 mg by mouth twice daily
- Prednisone 5 mg by mouth daily
Stopped: nintedanib. Home oxygen no longer needed.

Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: transplant clinic with frequent laboratory monitoring including tacrolimus levels; surveillance per program protocol. All medication changes go through the transplant team.

Lung Transplant Service

documents.title: Home
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted you to know I got the call in May and had the transplant. Home since the 2nd. Breathing without the oxygen for the first time in over a year. The transplant team is handling all my meds and labs, I have a binder the size of a phone book.

documents.title: Re: Home
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lloyd, this is wonderful news, thank you for telling me. We received your discharge summary last week. You're right to keep every medication question with the transplant team for now. I'm here for anything else, and we'll catch up in person once they give you the green light.

reports.text:
CHEST, PA AND LATERAL
Indication: fever, dyspnea and cough, 2 months after bilateral lung transplantation.
Comparison: none available at time of reading.
Findings: Postsurgical changes of bilateral lung transplantation. Diffuse interstitial infiltrates in both lungs. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal.
reports.conclusion: Diffuse interstitial infiltrates bilaterally after bilateral lung transplantation.

documents.title: Transplant pulmonary clinic note
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Transplant Pulmonary Clinic - copy to primary care
Date of service: 07/20/2026

Mr. Jacobs returns for scheduled follow-up of his IPF, now 2 months after bilateral lung transplantation, but today's visit is about two weeks of increasing breathlessness, a nonproductive cough and fevers. Recovery from surgery had been uneventful up to then. No sick contacts and no travel.

Medications: tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil and prednisone as at discharge.
Allergies: NKDA. Family history: father ILD, mother RA. Never smoker, 1-2 drinks/week before surgery, financial analyst.

Vitals: temperature 38.7 C (101.7 F), BP 130/85, heart rate 102, respiratory rate 26, SpO2 89% on room air.
Exam: crackles heard over both lungs.

Labs: WBC 9.0 K/uL, hemoglobin 12.5 g/dL, platelets 250 K/uL, creatinine 1.2 mg/dL, BUN 21 mg/dL, liver enzymes normal. CMV PCR positive.
Chest X-ray: diffuse interstitial infiltrates.

Impression: cytomegalovirus pneumonitis in a recent bilateral lung transplant recipient, with fever and hypoxemia.
Plan: direct admission to the transplant service today for IV ganciclovir and monitoring. Immunosuppression per inpatient team.

Transplant Pulmonary

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: lung transplant
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - Lung Transplant Service
Admitted: 07/20/2026 (direct from transplant clinic)  Discharged: 07/27/2026

Principal diagnosis: cytomegalovirus pneumonitis.
Background: bilateral lung transplantation 05/19/2026 for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.

Presentation: two weeks of dyspnea, dry cough and fever; in clinic 38.7 C, HR 102, RR 26, SpO2 89% on room air, bilateral crackles, diffuse interstitial infiltrates on chest film, CMV PCR positive.

Course: Started on IV ganciclovir 5 mg/kg every 12 hours on admission. Fever resolved and oxygen requirement fell over the following days. By discharge he was afebrile with SpO2 94% on room air. Transitioned to oral valganciclovir at treatment dose. Tacrolimus, mycophenolate and prednisone continued at the same doses.

Discharge medications:
- Valganciclovir 900 mg by mouth twice daily (new)
- Tacrolimus 2 mg by mouth twice daily, goal trough 8-12 ng/mL
- Mycophenolate mofetil 750 mg by mouth twice daily
- Prednisone 5 mg by mouth daily
Allergies: NKDA

Follow-up: transplant clinic in about 2 weeks; weekly CMV PCR and labs through the transplant program.

Lung Transplant Service

results.text: Detected, below the limit of quantitation

documents.title: Transplant clinic follow-up
documents.author: lung transplant
documents.body:
Lung Transplant Clinic - follow-up 08/13/2026

Seen 2.5 weeks after discharge for CMV pneumonitis. He feels much better, cough fading, no fevers at home. Afebrile in clinic, SpO2 95% on room air.
CMV PCR today: detected, below the limit of quantitation.

Plan: continue valganciclovir 900 mg twice daily with weekly CMV PCR until clearance, then the program will decide on the next step. Tacrolimus, mycophenolate and prednisone unchanged.

Lung Transplant Clinic

documents.title: Flu shot this year
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Getting my strength back after the CMV hospital stay. Question for the fall: am I still supposed to get a flu shot with all the transplant meds, and do I get it from you or from them?

documents.title: Re: Flu shot this year
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Good question. Yes, a flu shot is recommended, and it should be the regular injected kind (not the nasal spray). Transplant programs like to approve the timing, so please ask your coordinator when they want it. Once they okay it you're welcome to come here for it.
